prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 12 of 26 earlier cases, t = 0 in 14; when indemnified t per unit about 81 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per unit: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34)
- line 6 "Installer hours": no earlier line of this grade; level of the other hourly grades; when indemnified t per hr about 63 (80% range 23 to 176)
- line 8 "Service technician hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 47 (80% range 36 to 69); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), so this line (9 hr) about 425 (327 to 621)
- line 9 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 12 of 26 earlier cases, t = 0 in 14; when indemnified t per pc about 81 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34)

items.description: Close and repaint the disturbed wall area
items.rationale: The indoor supply-line leak falls under §2.4. Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(a) allow making good the access opening and repainting the disturbed patch; €285 gross allows for both tasks, not a whole-room repaint.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge on the building-services invoice. The gross estimate is €81 for one flat-rate charge.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows consumable sealing material used in the pipe repair. Allow €12 gross for one small supply.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow pipe matching the pre-loss specification. Allow €27 gross for the first metre attributed to the local repair.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows reinstatement of the original insulation at the repaired section. Allow €13 gross for one metre.
Section 7.1.7(g) allows reasonably necessary installation labour at customary rates. One hour at the gross prior rate of €63 gives €63.

Section 7.1.8(b) excludes the contractor’s own measuring devices, even though necessary diagnostic labour is covered under §7.1.7(e). If this were substantiated as a covered equipment deployment instead, allow €18 gross.
Section 7.1.7(e) and (g) allows necessary investigation and repair labour. The nine-hour gross benchmark is €425 for the whole entry.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only the first travel charge per contractor per invoice, regardless of the number of visits. The conditional benchmark for one otherwise eligible charge is €81 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and (e) allow necessary drying and one equipment deployment charge per drying operation. Allow €72 gross for the brief local deployment.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly treats the contractor’s blades as business overhead rather than repair materials. The conditional gross estimate for one blade is €12.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows compatible fittings used to connect the replacement pipe. Two ordinary fittings at €17 each give €34 gross.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (d) exclude duplicate charges and quantities not tied to the documented repair. If a distinct second metre was required and installed, allow €27 gross.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (d) exclude overlapping insulation charges unless this shell was needed for a distinct repaired length. If separately substantiated, allow €14 gross for one metre.

Sections 7.1.8(c) and 7.1.7(g) bar duplicate labour and require reasonable hours; multiple visits alone do not substantiate a second identical nine-hour entry. If all nine hours were distinct and necessary, the gross benchmark is €425.
